The horseshoe construction stays short exact after applying a right exact functor
items.strategy: Apply the projective horseshoe lemma to get a degreewise split short exact sequence of resolutions. A right exact functor is additive, so it carries each split row to a split exact row, and the degreewise exactness reassembles into a short exact sequence of complexes.

items.title: The connecting map for left derived functors
The left derived connecting map is independent of the horseshoe resolution and lifts
items.strategy: Construct a compatible middle comparison between two chosen horseshoes with fixed end lifts. Use fixed-side horseshoe homotopy uniqueness for middle maps, and separately use projective comparison uniqueness for changes of the end lifts; naturality of homology's connector then makes the transported map independent of every choice.

items.title: Left derived functors form a homological delta functor
items.strategy: Use the horseshoe sequence after applying the functor and homology's connecting morphism to define the long exact sequence, then use the independence lemma to remove every horseshoe choice. Naturality comes from the natural long exact homology sequence, and the zeroth term is the earlier degree-zero recovery theorem.

items.title: Right derived functors form a cohomological delta functor
items.strategy: Dualize the left-derived argument with injective horseshoes and the cohomology connecting morphism. The resulting long exact sequence is natural, independent of the chosen injective data, and starts in degree zero with the original left exact functor.

items.title: Natural transformations of base functors give morphisms of derived delta functors
items.strategy: The previous page already gives degreewise natural transformations on derived objects. Compare the ladders built from those maps with the naturality squares for the homology and cohomology connecting morphisms to prove compatibility with every connecting map.

items.title: The derived long exact sequence
items.strategy: Unpack the two delta-functor theorems and print the resulting long exact sequences with the library's chosen homological and cohomological degree conventions.

items.title: Positive left derived functors are effaceable by projectives
items.strategy: Choose a projective epimorphism onto the object. The map in positive derived degree factors through the corresponding projective value, and that source vanishes by the earlier derived-functor theorem, so the induced map is zero.

items.title: Positive right derived functors are effaceable by injectives
items.strategy: Choose an injective monomorphism out of the object. In positive cohomological degree the induced map lands in a value on an injective object, and that value vanishes, so the map is zero.

items.title: Dimension shift for a homological delta functor effaced in the middle
items.strategy: Inspect the exact segment around T_n(P) -> T_n(A) -> T_{n-1}(K) -> T_{n-1}(P). If both outer terms vanish, the connecting map is an isomorphism; if only one vanishes, the same exact segment yields the corresponding injectivity or surjectivity statement.

items.title: Dimension shift for a cohomological delta functor effaced in the middle
items.strategy: Read the exact segment around T^{n-1}(I) -> T^{n-1}(C) -> T^n(A) -> T^n(I). When the two terms involving I vanish, the connecting map becomes an isomorphism, and the one-sided vanishing cases give the promised monomorphism or epimorphism conclusions.

items.title: A partial morphism of delta functors extends through one dimension shift
items.strategy: Starting from an already compatible partial family through the preceding degrees, choose one effacement of the object and use the resulting monic connecting map or cokernel presentation to define the next-degree component. Keep the local construction and covered-ladder naturality separate from the later independence-of-effacement obligation.

items.title: The effacement extension is independent of the effacing morphism
items.strategy: Given two projective or injective effacements of the same object, compare them through their finite biproduct over that object. The one-step extension defined from the common dominating effacement restricts to the same map on both original choices.

items.title: The effacement extension commutes with connecting morphisms
items.strategy: Build the next-degree map from the dimension-shift square on the chosen effacements, then compare the two routes around the diagram defining the connecting morphism. The one-step construction and its choice-independence force the connecting square to commute.

items.title: Effaceable homological delta functors are universal
items.strategy: Induct on degree. Use a projective effacement and the dimension-shift lemma to define the next component, item 20 to show it is independent of the effacement, and item 21 to preserve compatibility with connecting morphisms; uniqueness comes from the same quotient presentation at each step.

items.title: Effaceable cohomological delta functors are universal
items.strategy: Repeat the universality induction with injective effacements. The next-degree component is defined through the cohomological dimension-shift isomorphism, made choice-free by the biproduct comparison lemma, and shown compatible with every connecting morphism by item 21.

items.title: Derived functors are universal delta functors
items.strategy: Combine the theorems that derived functors carry delta-functor structures with the effaceability propositions, and then apply the two universality theorems.

items.title: Universal delta functors extending the same degree-zero functor are uniquely isomorphic
items.strategy: Apply universality twice to the identity of the common degree-zero functor. The two induced morphisms are inverse because each composite is a universal self-map whose degree-zero part is the identity.

items.title: A morphism between universal delta functors is determined in degree zero
items.strategy: Universality says there is only one extension of a given degree-zero natural transformation, so two morphisms with the same degree-zero part must agree in every degree.

items.title: An exact base functor has the trivial universal delta functor
items.strategy: An exact functor has zero higher derived functors and recovers itself in degree zero. Since the derived delta-functor is universal, the only possible universal extension is the trivial one concentrated in degree zero.

items.title: Satellites give the first derived functor
items.strategy: Grothendieck's first satellite construction and the derived-functor construction are both universal extensions of the same degree-zero functor when the needed projective or injective effacements exist. The unique-isomorphism corollary therefore identifies the first satellites with L_1 and R^1.

items.title: Universality is the construction-independence principle
FALSE: any sequence of functors with long exact sequences is a delta functor
items.strategy: A delta functor is not just a family of exact sequences. The connecting maps must also be natural under morphisms of short exact sequences, so a degreewise exact family without those commutative squares does not qualify.

items.title: FALSE: effaceability means every positive value is zero
items.strategy: Use the effaceable left derived functors of tensoring with Z/n. Compute the first derived value at Z/n from its two-term free resolution, then transfer that nonzero value to the supplied resolution datum by comparison independence.

items.title: FALSE: a degree-zero natural transformation between delta functors always extends
items.strategy: Extension from degree zero is the content of universality, not part of the bare definition of a delta functor. The two universality theorems make the missing hypothesis explicit.

items.title: FALSE: the horseshoe connecting map is independent without a comparison proof
items.strategy: The connecting map for left derived functors is defined through chosen horseshoe resolutions. Without the explicit comparison argument, there is no reason for two different horseshoes to induce the same map on homology.

items.title: FALSE: universality removes the need for supplied resolution data
items.strategy: Universality compares delta-functor constructions after they have been built. It does not replace the earlier need to specify resolution data or to prove independence from those data before the comparison theorem applies.

items.title: Homology as a homological delta functor
items.strategy: Use the already-published long exact homology sequence for a short exact sequence of complexes as the concrete model of the abstract delta-functor definition.

items.title: The trivial delta functor of an exact functor
items.strategy: Take the exact functor in degree zero and zero in every positive degree. The previous proposition identifies this as the universal delta-functor attached to an exact base functor.

items.title: One dimension shift along a projective presentation
items.strategy: Apply the homological dimension-shift lemma to a short exact sequence 0 -> K -> P -> A -> 0 with P projective. The example writes the resulting isomorphism L_nF(A) ~= L_{n-1}F(K) and the one-sided consequences in low degrees.

items.title: One dimension shift along an injective copresentation
items.strategy: Apply the cohomological dimension-shift lemma to a short exact sequence 0 -> A -> I -> C -> 0 with I injective. The example records the resulting identification R^nF(A) ~= R^{n-1}F(C).

items.title: Extending a degree-zero natural transformation
items.strategy: Choose one projective or injective effacement of the object, compute the next-degree component by the dimension-shift square, and then point to the two follow-up lemmas that remove dependence on that choice and restore compatibility with connecting maps.

items.title: A nonnatural choice of connecting maps does not form a delta functor
items.strategy: Alter one connecting map in an otherwise exact family by a sign or automorphism chosen without functorial control. Exactness of the long sequence can survive, but at least one naturality square then fails.

items.title: Two universal delta functors and their unique isomorphism
items.strategy: Use the derived-delta theorem to identify both degree-zero terms with the same functor, then apply the unique-isomorphism corollary to the two universal extensions. The example emphasizes that the comparison is forced by degree zero, not by notation.
